reasons: Both answers correctly diagnose the base-mesh and quad-truncation bugs and give working evaluated-mesh, loop_triangles writers. B states plainly that 0.6 mm is too thin and cites 0.8 to 1.2 mm, while A calls it only borderline. B also covers the manifold check and normal orientation (the negative-scale winding flip), where A checks watertightness only. B's sanity check that compares the triangle count with base polygons is muddled, but that is a minor slip.

A: Suggests exporting a closed-bottom single surface for spiral vase mode; vase mode expects a closed solid, so a zero-thickness surface is not the right input
B: Says a triangle count of about 1x len(obj.data.polygons) means the modifier is missing; without Solidify the triangulated base mesh would still give about 2x
